Hi Amy / Dao,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great context on PayBoard's needs across Vietnam/Thailand and mid-market EU languages (Polish, Czech). Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Shortlist & rationale: based on your latency and budget targets, we recommend trying Redwood-6B-APQ (quantized) for throughput-sensitive paths, and Redwood-20B-QL (higher-precision) for customer-facing summaries in Polish/Czech. We also suggest an experimental run with open-llama-v2-13b-ptq for Thai to validate tokenization behavior.
- Benchmarks: I've attached the preliminary throughput/latency matrix and a short bench link (internal): https://redwood.company/benchmarks/linguatech-apac-2028 (also mirrored in the Drive link below).
- Prompt sets: shared a starter pack in Drive (prompt_pack_v1.zip) covering: invoice extraction, localized salutations, regulatory disclaimers in PL/CZ, and fallback prompts for short-context replies.
- Quality/regression concerns: you flagged hallucination on numeric fields during the demo — we'll include targeted evals that exercise numeric grounding and company-specific vocabulary (e.g., VAT IDs).

Action items:
1) Can you share the smaller sandbox dataset (5–10 example messages per locale) and the security questionnaire (you mentioned SOC2 evidence) so we can schedule a scoped pilot?
2) Are there internal stakeholders who should join the pilot kickoff? I propose a 45-min working session next week (TZ windows below).

Hi Ben,

Appreciate the clear write-up. A couple quick clarifications from our product team after the demo: 

- Data: we'll provide a sanitized sandbox of ~25 examples (across VI/TH/PL/CZ), not live customer data. Expect that file by EOD Friday.
- Security QA: attached the completed questionnaire (LinguaTech_Sec_Questionnaire.pdf). We need to confirm KMS/HSM options and an audit-log retention policy before we onboard for a pilot.
- Coverage: Polish and Czech are highest priority, but Thai tone/regionalization is critical for merchant-facing receipts. Do the tokenizers for Redwood-20B-QL require retraining for Thai word segmentation or do you rely on byte-level tokenizers?

Also, PayBoard's compliance lead (Jakub) asked whether you have a recommended threshold for numeric-extraction precision (we saw issues where invoice totals drifted by ~1–2%). If you can include an eval that tracks dollar/amount consistency across paraphrases, that would be helpful.

CC'ing Jakub to confirm the procurement window and whether we need an NDA addendum for the sandbox.

Thanks — Amy

Amy Tran

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-04T01:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Regional model candidate request & benchmarks

Thanks Amy — great questions. Quick technical clarifications: 

- Tokenization: Redwood runtimes use a byte-level tokenizer for Thai by default; for production-grade Thai normalization we recommend an upstream lightweight tokenizer layer (we can provide a reference script) that improves segmentation for receipt/merchant names. No model retrain required for the prompt-level fixes.
- Numeric extraction eval: we'll add a targeted bench using synthetic paraphrase sets + real sandbox examples to measure mean absolute error for amounts and a pass/fail on VAT formatting. Goal: <0.5% MAE for totals on the Redwood-20B-QL candidate; if not met we'll run targeted prompt templates that constrain numeric outputs.
- KMS/HSM & audit logs: Redwood Private supports customer KMS via AWS KMS or HashiCorp Vault; for the Hosted route we can enable envelope encryption and export audit logs to your preferred SIEM during the pilot.

Model shortlist (rationale + suggested role):
1) Redwood-20B-QL — primary for customer-facing summarization in PL/CZ (best accuracy on numerics, higher compute).
2) Redwood-6B-APQ — throughput-first for bulk ingest and autofill tasks (quantized path).
3) open-llama-v2-13b-ptq — test for Thai; lower licensing risk and good tokenization behaviour in our early experiments.

I've dropped a Drive folder with: prompt sets, synthetic numeric-paraphrase bench, and a lightweight tokenizer script for Thai. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB-Redwood/linguatech-eval-pack

Next steps we propose:
- Pilot scope doc: 2-week pilot, 3 locales, sample throughput target 250 qps for Redwood-6B-APQ path, 10 qps for Redwood-20B-QL.
- Kickoff: Ben — can you confirm the kickoff slot you'd like; we'll prepare a short eval plan and a runbook.

Thanks — Neha
